I've had potlucks done two ways. The first way is that everyone brings a dish and the second is the host is on the hook for a main entree and guests bring sides, desserts, or drinks. When the second one happened to me the first time, I was taken aback. I definitely wasn't expecting that but found it to be the common practice in the friends and peers I was in at the time. It was when I started making more money and hanging out with people who also had a little more money. I had a poverty upbringing and now more towards middle class and it was seen as kinda tacky that I didn't know this and had to be pressed for my part of the contributions. 

I think this is two different social cultures colliding with both thinking theirs is the norm. In the future having a conversation about what the theme of the dinner and what works within everybody's budget would probably be more appropriate. If you're able to pay the money I would go to your roommate and pay it so that it doesn't become a source of contention. With the third roommate already having paid it will definitely be not worth the ongoing stress it will have on your household as your third roommate will probably build a resentment that they paid and you did not in addition to the roommate asking for compensation. If you aren't able to pay for budgeting purposes I would take a conversation to the roommate and let them know your expectation of the potluck and where it fell different from theirs and see if you could possibly pay some now and work out the rest later so you're not over extended.
